question.text: When a PM evaluates the credit quality of a corporate bond independently, beyond the rating agency's view, the framework commonly used is the '4 Cs'. These are:

explanation.text: The Logic: Textbook 4 Cs of credit analysis: Capacity (repay), Collateral (security), Covenants (contractual protections), Capital (equity cushion). The Trap: The '4 Cs' is a finance-specific mnemonic; other students' mnemonics (Character, etc.) exist but textbook NISM uses this set. Cross-Exam Context: XV Ch 8 covers credit analysis; XXI-B expects fluency. Manager's Pro-Tip: Covenants are the most overlooked of the 4 Cs — a seemingly good issuer can have weak covenants that leave bondholders exposed in distress.
